doc.title: Al Tinney interviewed by Monk Rowe, Buffalo, New York, October 14, 2002

title: Society bands: Teddy Wilson at Cafe Society and Lester Lanin
summary: He arranged for Wilson's Cafe Society band and liked Lanin's band playing from their heads.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel

blocks.x: Was — some of the names like Lester Lanin, was that the type of society bands you would play in or was it smaller groups?

No. Now let me see now. Teddy Wilson had a band at Café Society that I did some arrangements for and it was not a Lombardo type thing, you know. It was just cool, you know, and it wasn’t exhibition or anything like that. It was just playing nice music. I liked the society music. Especially Lester Lanin, he had a band who never had any arrangements of anything in front of him, they all played from their heads.
That’s right. No music. They had their own heads and things they would play with.
I see. Each like horn man would have a role to play? © Fillius Jazz Archive -18-
